And I think it's because of one simple thing.

The companies may be using the physics engines for hit detection. I mean,you have physical objects flying around and bullet trajectories to calculate so it seems like a good short cut,right? Until you realize physics engines,even today,are buggy as hell and prone to massive glitches.

So we end up with lots of games that don't seem to function properly because of bad hit detection. Which is why you see lots of bunny hopping in games these days. Bunny hopping is a simple method to take advantage of crap hit detection. See,the more movement the hit detection system has to deal with,the more likely it is to fuck itself to death and not work right. So,any extra movement and it's more likely it won't register hits on you,making you at least partially invincible.
